inputs.spec: Interaction spec — the opt-in at checkout

documents.title: Interaction spec — the opt-in at checkout
documents.content:
Interaction spec — the opt-in at checkout
4 states, 6 transitions, 5 edge states, 3 open questions

## States
- Unasked — the delivery step with the switch off and the phone field hidden; the person can turn it on or continue without it.
- Asked — the switch on, the phone field shown and focused, Continue disabled until the field validates; the person can type, turn the switch off, or continue once valid.
- Saved — the review step shows "Reminder: <number>" with Change; the person can change or place the order.
- Declined — the review step shows no reminder line; the person can go back to add one.

## Transitions
| From | Action | To | What changes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unasked | turn the switch on | Asked | phone field appears, focused; Continue disables |
| Asked | type a valid number | Asked | Continue enables |
| Asked | type an invalid number | Asked | "[validation copy]" under the field; Continue stays disabled |
| Asked | turn the switch off | Unasked | field hides, its value kept for this session |
| Asked | Continue (valid) | Saved | review shows the number |
| Unasked | Continue | Declined | review shows no reminder line |

## Edge states
- Empty: the field shows the country code as a placeholder — assumed.
- Loading: saving past a second shows Continue as busy — assumed.
- Error: the number cannot be saved — "[error copy]" above Continue, the value kept — spec ("errors are shown inline").
- Partial: not applicable, one field.
- Return: back from review to delivery keeps the switch and number — assumed.

## Open questions
- If the person already has a number on their account: prefill or ask? The spec is silent.
- Is the switch on by default for returning customers? "opts in" suggests off; confirm.
- The validation copy and the error copy are not in the spec.

call.title: Usability test — order reminders by SMS
call.content:
Usability test — order reminders by SMS
4 tasks; 5 sessions read; top finding: 3 of 5 missed the reminder switch

## Tasks
1. You are buying a mug for a friend and want a text the day before it arrives. Get to the point where you are sure you will get one. — Success: the review step shows "Reminder: <number>".
2. You typed your number wrong. Fix it. — Success: the review step shows the corrected number.
3. You changed your mind and do not want texts. Make sure you will not get one. — Success: the review step shows no reminder line.
4. You have placed the order. Find out when the text will come. — Success: the confirmation names the day.

## Script
- Welcome: "We are testing the checkout, not you; nothing you do is wrong. Please think out loud as you go."
- Each task read verbatim; if silent for ten seconds: "What are you thinking?"; if stuck for a minute: "What would you expect to happen here?" then move on and note a fail.
- Close: "What was the hardest part? What would you change?"

## Measures
- Per task: completed alone / with a hint / failed; seconds to first action; where they hesitated; one quote.
- Sheet columns: session, task, result, first action (s), hesitation, quote.

## Findings
- The reminder switch on the delivery step — 3 of 5 scrolled past it; two found it on the review step's Change with a hint, one failed. "I thought that was the newsletter thing." (Task 1)
- The phone field's country code — 2 of 5 typed the leading zero and got the validation message; both fixed it. "Oh, it wants it without the zero." (Task 1)
- Seen once: one participant looked for the reminder in the confirmation email rather than the page (Task 4).

script.say:
4 tasks; 5 sessions read; 3 of 5 missed the reminder switch on the delivery step.

## Report
- read the interaction spec and the session notes; wrote "Usability test — order reminders by SMS"
